_comment: One TTFV receipt per reader per track. Fill by hand following docs/measurement/ttfv-protocol.md; delete no keys. Null means not reached, not applicable, or unknown. Save as docs/measurement/receipts/YYYY-MM-DD-<handle>-<track>.json. track: demo | own-agent. date: YYYY-MM-DD of the attempt. facilitator: a handle only, no personal data. network: yes | no, whether the machine had internet access during the attempt; required yes for Track A and for uv tool install; checked once before the clock starts (protocol 2.7). coaching_events: list of {"at", "what"}. failures: list of {"at", "milestone", "what"}, kept even when the attempt failed.

reader._comment: handle: a public handle, no other personal data. kind: cold | maintainer | ai-agent; only cold receipts without coaching events count toward cold-reader metrics.

machine._comment: os and cpu as reported by the system (e.g. uname -sr, CPU model and core count); python and uv are `python3 --version` and `uv --version`. uv_cache: cold (fresh UV_CACHE_DIR) or warm.

package._comment: version: the agent-reliability-ci version installed. source: pypi or wheel. wheel_sha256: required when source is wheel (record UV_FIND_LINKS and any UV_CACHE_DIR in notes, protocol 2.3). readme_url: the README read, at a fixed commit.

project._comment: Track B only; null for demo. kind: own | sample. description: what the agent is, or which recipe the sample tree came from. refs_preexisting: baseline, candidate, toolset and oracle were importable before the clock started. workers: worker count of the run.
project.description: examples/recipes/python_agent copied to a temporary directory, arci.yaml removed; project dir <tmp>

timestamps._comment: ISO 8601 with timezone, e.g. 2026-10-20T09:15:02Z. Track A uses readme_opened, command_start, demo_banner, demo_verdict, all_steps_held, interpretation_answered. Track B uses readme_opened, install_start, install_done, scaffold_start, descriptor_written, run_start, verdict_printed, store_validated, interpretation_answered. Leave the others null.

durations_seconds._comment: Whole seconds derived from the timestamps as the protocol defines per track (sections 3 and 4). agent_execution is Track B only: the sum of usage.wall_seconds over trials.jsonl in the run store (protocol 4.2), never subtracted from total.

outcome._comment: completed: every stop condition of the track held. verdict: PASS | BLOCK | INCONCLUSIVE | ERROR; Track B: the verdict stamped as verdict_printed; ERROR if none; Track A: the verdict for agent B. store_validated, decision_sha256, init_attempts, descriptor_hand_edited, trials_started: Track B only (protocol 4.3 and 4.6). descriptor_hand_edited: arci.yaml edited by hand before the run that produced the verdict, or, with no valid verdict, before any arci run that started trials. trials_started: trials.jsonl in the run store (protocol 4.2) exists and is non-empty. interpretation_correct is scored with the key in protocol 5.3.
outcome.interpretation_answer: INCONCLUSIVE (exit 2) means I did not get enough evidence either way. Both arms passed 8/8 in my 8-trial smoke run, and the interval on the difference was [-0.42, 0.42], which crosses the margin. It does not say the candidate is fine, and it does not say it regressed. The tool itself says that two perfect arms cannot PASS below N=42, so it was expected. It is not a green result and CI stays non-green. Also, my scaffold had only a clean condition with no injected fault, so it tested very little.

comprehension._comment: Answered once per reader, on the first track's receipt; on a second-track receipt set answered_on to that file name and leave the rest empty. Answers verbatim; scores per the key in protocol section 5; scorer is not the reader and is a handle only, no personal data. q2_who_for keeps its name for schema stability; it holds the whole q2 answer (who it is for and what the agent must expose).

coaching_events.what: Before readme_opened (not stamped): the facilitator prompt stated that this harness blocks `uv tool install` and that uvx or a uv venv are alternatives; it also prescribed the timestamping wrapper and the milestone names. No explanation of ARCI was given.

notes: Install method: uv venv .venv + uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python agent-reliability-ci (README's `uv tool install agent-reliability-ci` was denied by the harness). Commands: date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ ; uv tool install agent-reliability-ci (blocked, twice: once inside a compound command, once alone) ; uv venv .venv ; uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python agent-reliability-ci ; arci init checkout-retry --baseline app.v1:run --candidate app.v2:run --toolset tests.world:make_world --oracle tests.world:passed (attempt 1, exit 3, KeyError order_id) ; arci init checkout-retry --baseline app.v1:run --candidate app.v2:run --toolset tests.world:make_world --oracle tests.world:passed --task '{"order_id": "order-7"}' (attempt 2, exit 0) ; arci run arci.yaml | tee run.log (exit 2) ; ls runs/checkout-retry ; shasum -a 256 runs/checkout-retry/decision.json ; arci gate runs/checkout-retry (exit 2) ; shasum -a 256 runs/checkout-retry/decision.json ; find .. -name decision.json (to locate the store) ; bash -c 'uvx --from agent-reliability-ci arci demo ... echo exit: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}' (second demo run, only to capture the exit code). Store: <tmp> with decision.json, events.jsonl, manifest.json, trials.jsonl; gate line: VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE (exit 2). readme_opened is the Track A stamp (one README read for both tracks). store_validated stamp and the protocol 4.4 total are null (the reader validated the store itself; the facilitator did not stamp it). agent_execution summed from the store's trials.jsonl by the builder. AI-agent reader (Claude sonnet via the Workflow tool, persona: a product-minded developer who skims documentation and wants the fastest path to a result); self-stamped milestones with `date -u` under the facilitator's wrapper; machine shared with the orchestrator session (not controlled). Never counted as a cold reader. Protocol 2.1 deviation: the maintainer checkout was present on the machine; the reader read README.md from it and Track B copied the sample tree from it (no clone was made by the reader). Files read: README.md (lines 1-60 and 250-480 directly; the rest, 61-250, I only saw through truncated previews or skipped), examples/recipes/python_agent/ (copied; I listed the files app/__init__.py, app/v1.py, app/v2.py, tests/__init__.py, tests/world.py, README.md but did not open their contents), I did not open any docs/ file (DESCRIPTOR.md, REAL_AGENTS.md and others are linked but I did not read them). Confusions: The README gave me the whole path through one chained command (`uv tool install ... && arci init ... && arci run arci.yaml`) and also as three separate commands. Step 2 as written failed with KeyError: 'order_id'. Nothing before it told me that my toolset needs a task. The fix is `--task`, which is mentioned only later in a paragraph. I guessed the value {"order_id": "order-7"} from the example YAML. A skimmer would not know what value to use for their own agent. | The README says 'Replace these example references with your project's importable Python functions', but it does not say that arci init must be run from the project root, or that the task must be accepted by your own toolset. | `arci run arci.yaml` does not print where the run store is. The default is ./runs/<experiment_id>/. I found it by running `arci run --help` and `find`. The task's ls/shasum/gate step needed a store path I had to hunt for. | The demo's wrapper line used ${PIPESTATUS[0]}, which is bash-only. My shell is zsh, so 'exit:' printed empty. I re-ran the demo in bash to get the exit code (0). | The README states a runtime of 38 s on a fast Mac, or 72 s through uvx. My demo took about 74 s from start to the 'All six steps held' line, with uvx environment creation taking about 1 s, so it was consistent. | The README's 'Advanced: the Python manifest builder' section is empty, and the 'GitHub Actions' heading follows it directly. | The default scaffold has only a clean condition, with no fault, so the run is nearly guaranteed to be INCONCLUSIVE. It is explained, but the first three commands lead the reader to a result that tells them nothing about their agent. | `uv tool install agent-reliability-ci` is the README's install route and was denied by the harness. I used a venv instead.. Reader notes: Machine: macOS, load average about 3.3 at the start. The busiest processes were WindowServer and Claude app helpers. No other arci processes were seen. Python in my venv was CPython 3.13.12, even though 3.14 is on PATH. The run directory for Track A is <tmp> and it has demo.log. The demo's own run stores were in <tmp> Track B is in <tmp>, with the store in runs/checkout-retry/. Timestamps in Track A: banner 12:18:04Z, first VERDICT 12:18:27Z, last 'All six steps held.' 12:19:17Z. The gate's sha256 was identical before and after the `arci gate` run, which is read-only and exits 2, matching the run. I only saw the README through a persisted-output preview plus selected line ranges, so lines about 61-250 (evidence, 'where it has been run', 'the gate measured against itself') I read only partly. Not understood: how `arci plan` would pick a confirmatory N for my agent, what fault names are available, and what the sample project's agents actually do, because I did not open src/ or the sample sources. My interpretations of the verdicts come from the README table and the printed output."

failures.what: [at: 2026-10-13T12:19:2xZ (approximate, no date was run: both attempts happened between the Track B directory setup and the 12:19:31Z install_start)] First attempt, `uv tool install agent-reliability-ci` inside a compound command: 'Permission to use Bash with command ... has been denied.' A second attempt with the command alone gave the same message. I then chose the route `uv venv .venv` + `uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python agent-reliability-ci`, which worked. Note that the denial happened before any command ran, and I have no timestamp for it.

error: CliError: init: --toolset tests.world:make_world: calling it with the task and seed 0 raised KeyError: 'order_id'; check the toolset factory and --task (exit 3). Fixed by adding --task '{"order_id": "order-7"}' on the second attempt (12:19:40Z).
